title: getcheapapi: open-source agent skill for the cheapest SERP, X and SEO API calls
description: Free, MIT-licensed skill for Claude Code, Codex and other agents. Before each SERP, X, keyword or backlink call it prices every provider, uses the cheapest and stays under your budget. Change any route yourself.
og_desc: A free, open-source skill that makes your agent pay the lowest price for every API call.
og_alt: Same data, five prices. Your agent pays the lowest.
eyebrow: Open-source skill for AI agents · MIT
h1: Make your agent pay the lowest price for every API call.
lede: Add the skill to Claude Code, Codex or any agent. Before every SERP, X, Reddit, keyword or image call, your agent checks what each provider charges, uses the cheapest and stays under the budget you set. Everything is open: read every route and price, change them, or add your own provider.
cli_or: Scripts can use the CLI instead:
scroll_hint: See what your agent would save
fig1_aria: Figure: the same call priced by five routes, stepping down from what the default can cost to the lowest price, which is what your agent pays.
fig1_cap: same data, five prices · your agent pays the lowest
r_h2: Your agent is likely paying 2× to 200× more than it needs to.
r_sub: The same data costs very different amounts depending on who serves it, and the default route is usually the expensive one. This is the money you keep.
big_cap: Cheaper for the same X search, from the right source
led_batch: 15 calls where one batch would do
led_402: Requests sent after the balance ran out
led_foot: Your agent sees this before anything runs. Getting the quote is free.
w_h2: Lower bills, on terms you control.
f1_t: Your agent picks the lowest price
f1_d: It asks for serp.google, x.search or keyword.volume and gets the same fields whichever provider answers, so nobody compares price lists or rewrites code to switch.
f2_t: Know the cost before it pays
f2_d: Every run shows what each provider would charge, including the ones you have no key for, so you can tell whether another key would pay for itself.
f3_d: Set --max-usd and anything that would cost more is refused before it starts. The default cap is ten cents.
f4_t: It stops when the money runs out
f4_d: When a provider reports an empty balance (402), the run stops with exit code 2, and the skill tells your agent to stop instead of retrying hundreds of times.
f5_d: Prices are checked again right before each call. If the cheapest one jumps, the run waits for your OK.
f6_t: Fewer calls for the same data
f6_d: Duplicates are dropped and lists go out as one batch where the provider allows it, so you pay for each result once.
f7_t: Know exactly where the money went
f7_d: Every charge is logged on your machine. getcheapapi spend shows the total by provider and endpoint.
f8_d: Routes, field mappings, prices and the skill's own instructions are plain files in the repo. Nothing is hidden behind a hosted service.
f9_d: Add a provider, drop one, change a default cap or rewrite the skill's instructions. It is your copy: edit it and your agent uses it on the next call.
f10_t: Your keys and data stay with you
f10_d: No account and no middleman. Calls go straight from your machine to the provider, and the price cache and ledger stay local.
fig2_aria: Figure: the same job priced by five routes as bars of decreasing height; your agent pays for the shortest.
fig2_cap: same job, five prices · your agent pays for the shortest bar
c_h2: 15 kinds of data to start. Add your own.
c_sub: Ships with routes across AnyAPI, DataForSEO, GoAnyAPI, twitterapi.io and Yir. Need another provider or endpoint? Add it to the catalog in a few lines, and send a pull request if others could use it too.
c_caption: Data your agent can ask for, and the providers that sell it
i_h2: Free and open. Make it yours.
i_sub: Clone it, link the skill into your agent and add the keys you already have. Fork it, change it, ship it with your own agents.
li1: Agent skill for Claude Code, Codex and others
li2: CLI for scripts: quote, run, spend
li3: A catalog of routes and prices you can edit
li4: Budget caps and stop-on-402 built in
li5: A local ledger of every charge
li6: Works with one key; add more any time
li7: MIT: use it, fork it, ship it
a1: Yes. MIT licensed, with no account and no fee. You pay providers directly with your own keys, at their prices.
q2: Which agents does it work with?
a2: Any agent that can load a skill folder or run a shell command, such as Claude Code and Codex. Scripts and cron jobs can call the CLI directly.
q3: Can I add a provider or change a price?
a3: Yes. Routes and prices live in one catalog file. Edit it, run the free schema check against the live provider, and keep the change to yourself or send a pull request.
q4: Do I need a key for every provider?
a4: No. One key is enough to start. Routes you have no key for are still priced, so you can see what adding one would save.
q5: Does my data go through your servers?
a5: No. There are no servers of ours in the path. The price cache, ledger and saved results stay in ~/.getcheapapi on your machine.
a6: It depends on the data and how much of it you buy. Run getcheapapi quote with your own input: it shows every provider's price side by side and spends nothing.
ft_tag: Open-source agent skill that sends every data and media API call down the cheapest route. Free, and yours to change.
